reviewer: Interaction and accessibility A; continuation of the refinement reviewer
scope: Refined V5 local review studio; source and recorded evidence, before reading B
opinion: Preserve the corrected interaction foundation. Recorded keyboard and pointer activation now move focus with the viewport to the visible heading, then Tab stays in the player. Collection advance retains its initiating focus; pause, rest, wraparound and reduced-motion inspection have captured results. The visible heading ring is supported by both screenshot and computed-style evidence. These resolve the earlier demonstrated defects, without establishing comprehensive accessibility.
scoreReason: Not yet scored: the predecessor issued a bounded verdict without a numerical baseline. A new score would require resolving the shortcut context and native-selection evidence gaps; absence of those checks is not a demonstrated accessibility failure.

deductions.kind: source-supported interaction risk; not browser-reproduced here
deductions.effect: The document listener cancels Space and changes playback for BODY/H2/P targets. It also changes feelings on arrows outside native controls. Existing native-control exemptions do not establish ordinary page-reading behavior; no visible shortcut instruction appears in index.html.

criteriaForNine: Bound shortcuts to a deliberate, explained player interaction context, or remove them; verify ordinary reading keys do not operate the player.
Retain captured focus, playback and reduced-motion improvements with fresh regression evidence after changes.
Complete a genuine native keyboard selection and a bounded assistive-technology traversal; record actual outcomes and residual limits before considering a high scoped interaction score.
confidence: High for inspected source and recorded state transitions; moderate for overall local interaction quality.
limits: The native-key probe leaves Angry selected: neither successful selection nor a proven broken selector.
Viewport overflow checks establish geometry only. No human expression-recognition, real touch-device or accessibility-conformance claim.
